mappings.note: Share of the earth's surface that is land is a statement about how a natural resource is spread over the earth -> LO-1, not LO-2, since nothing about its use is asked.
Private land ownership. Ownership categories are neither uneven distribution (LO-1) nor judicious use (LO-2); the competency is the nearest legal code for classifying a resource by who holds it.
Common property resource example; the same ownership-classification gap -> competency.
Continent in which Tanzania lies, from the chapter's land-use case study. LO-4 covers locating countries on a world map but only for major crops, so the competency is cited for a plain location item.
What determines soil type; soil formation is descriptive and is covered by neither LO-1 nor LO-2 -> competency.
Weathering named as the breakdown of exposed rock; a soil-formation process -> competency, same gap.
Composition of soil; descriptive -> competency.
Mass movement of rock downhill signals a landslide, which LO-9 names explicitly.
Ranking which natural resource matters most; a judgement about resources in general, not their distribution or a conservation case -> competency.
Uneven population distribution explained by the characteristics of land -> LO-8, the only outcome about population distribution.
Which soil horizon supports vegetation; soil-profile description -> competency.
Overgrazing as a cause of land degradation is the case against unjudicious use of soil -> LO-2, not LO-1.
Soil conservation method -> LO-2, which names soil explicitly.
Rock piling to slow water flow is a soil-conservation technique -> LO-2.
Mulching to retain soil moisture -> LO-2 soil conservation.
Water wasted by a dripping tap is the classic argument for judicious water use -> LO-2.
Cause of evaporation; a water-cycle fact rather than a conservation or distribution claim -> competency.
Definition of the biosphere; descriptive -> competency, since neither LO-1 nor LO-2 covers defining the life zone.
The life-supporting system named; definitional -> competency.

Species protected under CITES is wildlife conservation. LO-2 names water, soil and forest rather than wildlife, but conservation of a natural resource is its substance and no other outcome reaches it; the wording gap is noted.

Low-lying areas being flood-prone is a natural-hazard item. LO-9 and C-SST2.2 list only forest fire, landslide and industrial disasters, so floods have no outcome; the goal, which speaks of natural and human-made disasters generally, is the honest citation.
Which regions are sparsely populated -> LO-8 population distribution.
Average per-person water consumption; a figure used to argue for judicious water use -> LO-2.
Causes of Yamuna pollution; degradation of a water resource, the case LO-2 argues against.
Common property resource again (duplicate of qid:110133) -> competency.

Terrace farming in hilly regions is presented here as a soil-conservation measure -> LO-2. LO-3 (types of farming) was considered but the chapter and the item frame it as erosion control, not as an agricultural practice being described.
A named way to prevent soil erosion -> LO-2.
The major threat to the environment (land degradation / deforestation) -> LO-2's conservation case.
Heavy rain causing landslides in mountains; LO-9 names landslides and their causes.
Which regions are densely populated -> LO-8.
Definition of land use; definitional and about a resource in general -> competency, not LO-1, which is about unevenness.
Factors determining land use are exactly why the resource is used unevenly across the earth -> LO-1.
Australia's dominant land use compared with other countries -> LO-1, the uneven pattern of resource use across the earth.
Lowest layer of the soil profile; descriptive -> competency.
Soil conservation method (duplicate theme of qid:110143) -> LO-2.
Which source is not groundwater; classifying water sources rather than conserving them -> competency.
Why forest cover should be increased -> LO-2, which names forest explicitly.
Causes of large-scale forest and arable-land destruction -> LO-2's case against unjudicious use.
Which landslide-mitigation technique does not apply -> LO-9's risk-reduction measures.
Distinguishing physical from human factors in land use -> LO-1, the analysis of why resource use differs across places.
Naming arable land; land terminology -> competency. LO-3 was considered but that outcome is about crops and farming practices, not about classifying land.
Meaning of land degradation -> LO-2, the harm judicious use is meant to prevent.
Second factor of soil formation alongside parent rock; descriptive -> competency.
Land used for grazing (pasture); land classification -> competency.
Types of land by ownership -> competency, the same ownership gap as qid:110132.
Which country Peter is from, in the chapter's land-use comparison. Pure case-study recall with no outcome of its own -> competency.
Shelter belts are a soil-conservation measure against wind erosion -> LO-2.
Biosphere reserves protect vegetation and wildlife; conservation of natural resources -> LO-2, with the same wildlife wording gap noted at qid:110150.
Water markets in India arise from water scarcity and its management -> LO-2, which names water.
